response:
Diagnosis. Gen 6 produced the archive's first signal strong on *both* axes: CollateralPoorDependence (fmb -4.23, ls_alpha -2.9%, t -2.87, sharpe -0.35). Cross-reading the whole archive, the structure that works is now precise: **a non-negative conditioning weight with broad cross-sectional support, multiplied by a contrast whose long side is explicitly the cash-rich firm.** The liquidity leg is the alpha engine and it is remarkably robust (-2.9% to -5.3%, t -2.9 to -5.6 across five different weights: issuance, deal intensity, capex, intangibility, near-term debt). The FMB slope appears only when the weight itself varies widely and monotonically (intangibility -4.23, capex -4.19); it vanishes when the weight is a narrow, near-degenerate quantity (TripleHurdle -0.17, UncoveredShare -0.69, NearTermObligations -0.60). And RealizedVersusLatentDependence is the decisive negative control: substituting a signed net-issuance leg for the cash rank preserved the slope (-4.03) but destroyed the alpha (+0.002), confirming that the abnormal return comes specifically from having cash-rich firms in the long tail, not from issuance. With two generations left I consolidate on this architecture, refining the weight's support and the definition of "resources," and keep two genuinely different constructions (a positive-side mirror and a persistence count) so the batch still teaches something new.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: CollateralShortfallDependence
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(at, ppent), at), 1)), SUB(IND_RANK(WINSOR(GROWTH(csho, 1), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, LAG(at, 1)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm with little pledgeable plant has no fallback if capital markets close, so raising equity from a thin cash position is far more dangerous for it than for a firm whose asset base could be borrowed against; the return penalty for market dependence should scale with the share of assets that cannot serve as collateral.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The best joint performer used intangible intensity as its weight, but intan is exactly zero for a large share of firms, which compresses half the cross-section into an uninformative band; the non-pledgeable share of assets is the same economic concept with full support at every firm and does not coincide with the documented intangible-intensity predictor. Everything else is held fixed, so this isolates weight support — the design choice the archive says determines whether the FMB slope materializes.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: MarketAccessClaimsVersusLiquidity
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(at, ppent), at), 1)), SUB(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(GROWTH(csho, 1), RATIO(dlc, LAG(at, 1)))), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, LAG(at, 1)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Two very different things force a firm back to the capital market — new equity it is currently raising and old debt about to mature — and both should be measured against the same liquid buffer; a collateral-poor firm whose combined market-access needs exceed its cash is the purest case of externally dependent expansion.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The two largest alphas in the archive came from pairing cash against equity issuance (-5.3%) and against near-term maturing debt (-5.3%), but neither combined them, and they are economically complementary rather than redundant: one is voluntary market access, the other is compelled. Pooling them by rank before contrasting with cash keeps the leg bounded and monotone, and the collateral weight supplies the broad support that generates the cross-sectional slope.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: IntangibleDependenceFullResources
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(intan, at), 1)), SUB(IND_RANK(WINSOR(GROWTH(csho, 1), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(che, ADD(dvc, prstkc)), LAG(at, 1)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: The relevant internal buffer is not just cash on hand but cash plus the distributions the firm chose to make, because a firm handing money back to shareholders while issuing shares plainly had resources it did not need to raise; widening the resource definition should sharpen the separation between genuinely dependent and merely active issuers.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This holds the archive's best-performing weight and contrast structure fixed and varies only the definition of internal resources, the one component that has never been tested against the pure cash stock in this architecture. The addition is economically motivated rather than mechanical — distributions are revealed evidence of funding capacity — and it should move firms that both issue and distribute out of the short tail, which is where the FinancingChurn evidence suggests the interpretation is muddiest.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: CashRichSelfFundedInvestor
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, LAG(at, 1)), 1)), SUB(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(capx, LAG(ppent, 1)), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(GROWTH(csho, 1), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: The mirror image of the archive's result should hold: among liquidity-rich firms, those investing heavily without going to shareholders are funding real opportunities out of their own resources and should earn high returns, while liquidity-rich firms issuing shares without investing are timing the market.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every profitable construction so far has put cash on the long side of a contrast; this rearranges the same three ingredients so that liquidity is the conditioning weight and the contrast is investment-versus-issuance, which tests whether the effect is about liquidity as a state or liquidity as a funding source. It is also the batch's only positive-signed proposal, and its long tail is cash-rich self-funded investors rather than dividend payers, avoiding the construction that repeatedly produced wrong-signed FF5 alphas.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: OutsideFundingBreadthCapex
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(capx, LAG(ppent, 1)), 1)), SUB(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(lt, ADD(dltt, dlc)), 1), LAG(at, 1)), GROWTH(csho, 1))), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, LAG(at, 1)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Non-interest-bearing operating credit and new equity are both outside money that a capital-spending firm can lean on, and a firm funding its program from either while holding no liquid buffer is dependent regardless of which of the two it used.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: SupplierFundedCapex delivered a strong alpha (-3.1%, t -3.35) but a weak slope (-1.57), and the natural diagnosis is that operating-liability growth alone is a narrow, noisy funding channel; pooling it with equity issuance broadens the funding leg without abandoning the supplier-credit insight. This also partially addresses the critic's concern that the leg is a pure operating-liability sort, since a firm scoring high must be short of cash while funded from at least one outside source.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: ChronicDependenceCount
EXPRESSION: TS_SUM(MIN(INDICATOR(WINSOR(GROWTH(csho, 1), 1), 0.02), INDICATOR(SUB(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), LAG(at, 1)), RATIO(che, LAG(at, 1))), 0)), 3)
HYPOTHESIS: Being externally dependent for one year can be a lumpy project; being dependent for three years running is a business model, and chronic dependence identifies firms whose expansion has never been validated by internally generated resources.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The archive measures the dependent state only contemporaneously; this counts how many of the last three years the firm was simultaneously issuing equity and running an investment program larger than its cash balance, using MIN as a logical AND on the two indicators. It is a discrete, slow-moving state variable, which should give far more stable portfolio composition than the annual-flow constructions whose deciles turn over every year, and its long tail is firms that have never been in the dependent state.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---CRITIQUE CollateralShortfallDependence---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The weight (at−ppent)/at includes cash and receivables, so the "non-pledgeable" measure mechanically rises with the very liquidity the contrast leg subtracts — an internal inconsistency with the "no fallback if markets close" story — and beyond that it is a single-ingredient weight swap on the archive's CollateralPoorDependence.

---CRITIQUE MarketAccessClaimsVersusLiquidity---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Pooling voluntary issuance with maturing short-term debt against a common cash buffer is economically sensible, but it inherits the same cash-contaminated collateral weight and is otherwise a mechanical union of two already-evaluated archive legs (CollateralPoorDependence and NearTermObligationsDuringExpansion) rather than a new mechanism.

---CRITIQUE IntangibleDependenceFullResources---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This changes exactly one addend inside one leg of an existing archive signal, adding flow variables (dvc, prstkc) to a stock (che) in the same normalized ratio — a dimensionally sloppy and cosmetic variant whose "revealed funding capacity" content was already probed by UncoveredShareOfProgram.

---CRITIQUE CashRichSelfFundedInvestor---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The positive-sign self-funding economics has already been tested twice in this archive (PayoutFundedInvestment, SelfFundedVersusMarketFundedGate) and produced a wrong-signed FF5 alpha, and the long leg — cash-rich, high-capex, non-issuing firms — simultaneously loads on the documented cash-holdings premium and against the well-known investment/asset-growth anomaly, so a positive result would be hard to attribute to the stated mechanism.

---CRITIQUE OutsideFundingBreadthCapex---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The diagnosis (operating-liability growth is a narrow, noisy single funding channel) is stated correctly and the fix — broadening the outside-money leg to any external source while keeping the cash contrast and capex weight — is a substantive rather than cosmetic response, though the incremental content over SupplierFundedCapex is modest and its two pooled legs may simply average a strong and a weak effect.

---CRITIQUE ChronicDependenceCount---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Recasting external dependence as a persistent state via a three-year AND-count is a genuinely different measurement axis from the archive's contemporaneous flow interactions and should stabilize portfolio composition, but the signal takes only four discrete values, which will coarsen the cross-sectional sort and limit the achievable FMB slope, and it partially overlaps SerialIssuerInvestmentProgram's multi-year indicator design.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: BorrowingHeadroomDependence
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(ppent, lt)), 1)), SUB(IND_RANK(WINSOR(GROWTH(csho, 1), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, LAG(at, 1)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: What makes market dependence bite is having no debt capacity left: a firm whose pledgeable plant is small relative to the claims already outstanding cannot borrow if equity markets close, so cash-poor equity issuance by such a firm is genuinely forced, whereas a firm with plant far exceeding its liabilities always retains a secured-borrowing fallback.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The weight is now collateral measured against existing claims rather than asset composition, so it excludes cash entirely and is not contaminated by the liquidity the contrast leg subtracts — it is itself a cross-theme quantity (pledgeable investment assets versus total financing claims) and is economically distinct from the intangible-intensity predictor. It also has full continuous support across the cross-section, which the archive shows is the condition under which this architecture produces a cross-sectional slope as well as an alpha.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: ErraticProgramDependence
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(VOL(WINSOR(RATIO(capx, LAG(ppent, 1)), 1), 5)), SUB(IND_RANK(WINSOR(GROWTH(csho, 1), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, LAG(at, 1)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Outside investors cannot discipline a spending program they cannot predict: firms whose investment rate swings wildly from year to year give suppliers of capital no benchmark, so when such a firm funds itself with equity from a thin cash position the money is most likely to be misallocated, while a steady-state investor's external funding is verifiable against a stable plan.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Every conditioning weight tried so far is a level or a composition measure; this one is the second moment of the *investment* program, which is a different economic quantity from the financing volatility tested earlier (UnstablyFundedInvestment, which measured issuance instability and gave a wrong-signed alpha). It has broad continuous support by construction, and it identifies the population where monitoring is hardest rather than merely restating who invests or who issues.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: TotalFundingCapacityGap
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), LAG(at, 1)), 1)), SUB(IND_RANK(WINSOR(GROWTH(csho, 1), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(che, ppent), lt), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm's true internal funding capacity is its liquid balance plus what its pledgeable assets can support net of the claims already against them; issuing equity while that whole capacity is thin is the state that reveals dependence, whereas issuing while capacity is ample is discretionary.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Rather than adding payout flows to a cash stock — the dimensionally sloppy change the critic rejected — this replaces the resource leg with a single stock-consistent measure of net pledgeable liquidity (cash plus plant less total liabilities), which brings debt capacity into the definition of internal resources for the first time in this archive. The investment-intensity weight is retained unchanged so the comparison against the existing cash-only formulation is clean, and both tails remain heavy investors.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: PeakProgramFundingGap
EXPRESSION: MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), LAG(at, 1)), TS_MAX(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), LAG(at, 1)), 5)), 1), SUB(IND_RANK(WINSOR(GROWTH(csho, 1), 1)), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, LAG(at, 1)), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Externally funded expansion is most dangerous at the top of a firm's own spending cycle, when commitments are maximal and reversal is costly; a firm running its largest program in five years on outside money from an empty balance sheet is at maximum overextension, while the same funding position at the bottom of its own cycle carries little commitment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This abandons the positive-side self-funding construction the critic correctly noted has already failed twice and instead supplies the one weight the archive has evidence for but never implemented continuously — within-firm cycle position, which produced the strongest FMB slopes when coarsely proxied by TS_RANK and MA deviations. Expressing it as the ratio of the current program to the firm's own five-year maximum gives a bounded, continuous, firm-demeaned weight that cannot be a restatement of the cross-sectional investment level, paired with the contrast that reliably carries the FF5 alpha.
